legend.planned: Planned or researched, not available yet

items.feature: Kohn-Sham DFT with plane waves
items.note: Periodic cells, norm-conserving pseudopotentials (UPF v2 subset), spin-unpolarized.

items.feature: LDA (Perdew-Zunger) and PBE (GGA)
items.note: PBE comes from the xcx library; tested against QE on the same pseudopotential.

items.feature: Insulators with fixed occupations
items.note: Fixed occupations require a sampled band gap. Use the separate Fermi-Dirac option for partial occupations.

items.feature: Gamma, Monkhorst-Pack grids (shifted or not), explicit k lists
items.note: Time reversal and opt-in crystal symmetry reduction; only model-, mesh- and FFT-grid-preserving operations. [Evidence](tests/reference/symmetry/evidence.json).

items.feature: Pulay and linear density mixing, block Davidson eigensolver
items.note: Strict runs use a fixed-point certificate and energy audit. Opt-in standard results are not certified.

items.feature: One TOML file; units (Ha, Ry, eV, Angstrom, Bohr, ...) and expressions such as 1/4 or 5.43/2 Angstrom
items.note: Wrong inputs are rejected with the key path of the problem.

items.feature: results.json (energies, eigenvalues, convergence history, provenance) and the electron density (binary + metadata)
items.note: Every run records input and pseudopotential hashes.

items.feature: Threads over k points and over bands, bit-identical results for any thread count
items.note: `[scf] threads = N`; default is 1.

items.feature: Agrees with Quantum ESPRESSO 7.6 on silicon (energies, eigenvalues, k grids, PBE)
items.note: See the validation results below. One cell and one pseudopotential so far.

items.feature: Band structures and density of states (CSV, SVG figure, QE-/VASP-style files)
items.note: `bands` and `dos` subcommands: CSV, SVG, QE- and VASP-style files. Fixed-density non-self-consistent calculation; checked by the repository tests.

items.feature: Electron density, ELF and potentials as cube, XSF, CHGCAR and VTK files
items.note: Cube, XSF, CHGCAR and VTK writers; opens in VESTA, VMD, ParaView and similar viewers. Checked against format specifications in tests.

items.feature: Convergence fix for larger cells (8-atom silicon cell stalled at the default settings)
items.note: Buffer bands: the highest requested bands are loosely converged; strict bands keep the full tolerance. The 8-atom silicon cell now converges.

items.feature: Input preflight check: element versus pseudopotential, SCF settings, plain-language summary of what will be computed
items.note: `validate` checks element versus pseudopotential and SCF settings and prints a plain-language summary; no SCF is run.

items.feature: Optional Intel MKL backend for FFT and matrix products, chosen at compile time
items.note: Merged behind a compile-time feature; the default build stays pure Rust. Kernel-level measurements on the test server look promising; end-to-end numbers follow.

items.feature: RMM-DIIS eigensolver for large band counts and Kerker-preconditioned mixing for hard cases (merged as switchable modules); cheaper FFT call structure (in progress)
items.note: Defaults are unchanged; a default changes only with evidence on several systems.

items.feature: Structure and input importers, Materials Project lookup, pseudopotential download with license and hash checks, a guided or natural-language style CLI
items.note: In design now.

items.feature: General benchmark and robustness suite (not silicon-only)
items.note: Used to judge speed and defaults on many cell shapes, band counts and pseudopotentials.

items.feature: Observable, controllable calculations for people and AI agents: step-by-step SCF, live events, safe-point policy changes, checkpoint/restart, self-healing SCF demo, MCP server, Python/ASE
items.note: Design in progress (docs/research/agent-native-directive-review.md); no runtime code yet. The numerical core stays free of LLM and network dependencies.

items.feature: Offline pseudopotential registry with license and SHA-256 checks
items.note: `pseudo` subcommands; pseudopotential files are never shipped in the repository.

items.feature: Fermi-Dirac occupations and chemical potential
items.note: Unpolarized and collinear finite-temperature SCF; analytic synthetic oracles and an Al smoke run, no QE metal comparison. Check empty-band convergence; finite-T restart unavailable. [Evidence](tests/reference/occupations/summary.json).

items.feature: Collinear spin with fixed up/down electron counts
items.note: LDA-PW and PBE; synthetic analytic and zero-moment oracles. No validated magnetic material ground state; noncollinear and spin-orbit remain unavailable. [Evidence](crates/dft-engine/tests/collinear-evidence.json).

items.feature: DFT+U, meta-GGA, hybrid functionals, dispersion corrections
items.note: Roadmap and validation oracles are in docs/research/xc-and-manybody-roadmap.md.

items.note: Independent header checks and synthetic NLCC oracles; Si/MgO bulk smoke, comparison with QE pending. Datasets remain unqualified; ultrasoft and PAW unavailable. [Evidence](tests/reference/datasets/p13c-status.json).

items.feature: Atomic forces
items.note: Strict NC LDA/PBE, NLCC, fixed spin and Fermi-Dirac; energy finite differences and independent scalar checks. DFT+U forces unsupported; comparison with QE pending. [Evidence](tests/reference/forces/manifest.json).

items.feature: Space-group symmetry (k-point reduction, density symmetrization)
items.note: Opt-in k-point reduction and density symmetrization; full/reduced, spin and finite-temperature checks. Magnetic spin swaps unsupported; comparison with QE pending. [Evidence](tests/reference/symmetry/evidence.json).

items.feature: RPA and cRPA correlation (research stage)
items.note: Design only; no implementation yet.

items.feature: Electronic-state landscape exploration: several self-consistent solutions, state comparison, branch tracking
items.note: Design in docs/roadmap/esle.md; starts after the baseline is complete.

items.feature: Coupling to outside environments (embedding, solvent, QM/MM, applied electric fields) through typed interfaces
items.note: Design in docs/architecture/scientific-coupling.md.

items.feature: GPU backends and MPI
items.note: Design study in progress; the CPU path stays the reference.

items.feature: Opt-in standard convergence profile
items.note: Strict remains default. Standard reduces solver work in stored successful cases but is not certified; skew/slab/mesh failures remain. [Evidence](tests/reference/perf/p17a/final-report.json).

items.feature: Stress and pressure
items.note: Strict NC frozen-basis strain derivatives; ASE strain check and separate Pulay estimate. Standard profile unsupported; real Si/MgO material stresses inconclusive; comparison with QE pending. [Evidence](tests/reference/stress/validation.json).

items.feature: Fixed-cell ionic relaxation
items.note: BFGS/FIRE, Cartesian constraints, warm starts and byte-identical restart. CLI spin-polarized and finite-temperature relaxation unsupported; Gamma-only MgO is not bulk qualification; comparison with QE pending. [Evidence](tests/reference/relaxation/manifest.json).

items.feature: Cell relaxation
items.note: Works for the stated synthetic cases and isotropic PseudoDojo Si/MgO shifted-mesh runs, with limits: rebuild plus fresh-basis polish verifies start agreement and final pressure. Full-tensor symmetry preservation on shifted meshes and cutoff convergence are not established; comparison with QE pending. [Evidence](tests/reference/relaxation/cell/validation.json).

can_today: Total energy, eigenvalues and electron density of insulating periodic systems with LDA or PBE, on Gamma or a k mesh.
Reproducible runs: the result files carry hashes, options and the energy audit.
not_yet: Validated magnetic and metallic material accuracy; DFT+U for correlated transition-metal oxides. Spin, NLCC and Fermi-Dirac options have limited validation below.
Spin-polarized or finite-temperature relaxation in the CLI, DFT+U forces, standard-profile stress, molecular dynamics, phonons and hybrid functionals.
speed: Measured on one server (dev08, 2 x Xeon Gold 6230, Rocky Linux 9.7, one socket, Intel MKL 2026.1 linked in both codes, same silicon pseudopotential and FFT grid; QE 7.6 with MPI, one thread per process), same session and idle node, 2026-11-05, BAANDI commit fdce016 for the k-point mesh and the later commit 7fe2e9a for the 8-atom cell (the k-point results did not change between them). Ratios are BAANDI time over QE time, so above 1 means BAANDI is slower. Silicon with a 4x4x4 shifted k mesh (2 atoms): at 8 to 16 cores 2.0 to 2.2 times slower than QE at convergence threshold 1e-8 and 1.4 to 1.6 times slower at 1e-12 (QE needs 8 instead of 5 iterations at 1e-12; both are reported because the ratio depends on it); on one core 4.2 to 5.1 times (1e-8). An 8-atom cell at Gamma only (one k point): against QE's complex k=0 path (`K_POINTS automatic 1 1 1`) BAANDI is 5.3 to 8.0 times slower on one core and 13 to 15 times slower at 16 cores; against QE's real-wavefunction Gamma path (`K_POINTS gamma`, QE's best configuration for this case, 1.3 to 1.9 times faster than its complex path and the reference for the goal of exceeding QE) BAANDI is 9.6 to 14.9 times slower on one core (1e-12 and 1e-8 convergence thresholds; MKL and pure Rust builds), (a machine-tuned build, `target-cpu=native`, makes the pure Rust build 1.1 to 1.4 times faster on dev08 with bit-identical results, bringing the one-core ratio to QE's real Gamma path down to 11.3; the ratios above use the default portable build) because BAANDI's threading speeds this case up only 1.4 times at 8 threads, it has no real-wavefunction Gamma path yet, and it performs more eigensolver work per SCF iteration; this is the main known weakness and is being worked on. Cases where QE takes under 0.3 s are excluded: QE's timer resolves only 0.01 s. The numbers were relayed from the measuring session and have not been independently reproduced here; build hashes, raw tables and limits: tests/reference/perf/dev08_final_relayed.md.
